title: Sorting Three Groups
summary: Given an integer array where each element is either 1, 2, or 3, determine the least number of elements to remove to ensure the array is in non-decreasing order.
statement: Given an integer array where each element is either 1, 2, or 3, determine the least number of elements to remove to ensure the array is in non-decreasing order. In each operation, one element can be deleted.
constraints: Return the minimum changes needed to make nums nondecreasing.
hints: A nondecreasing prefix ending in value v may follow only states at most v.
Track minimum changes for prefixes ending in one, two, or three.
For each value, take the allowed prefix minimum plus whether changing the current element is necessary.
The three states exhaust the possible final group of every nondecreasing transformed prefix.
editorial: The three states exhaust the possible final group of every nondecreasing transformed prefix.

tests.explanation: Changing three positions can produce a nondecreasing grouping of ones, twos, then threes.
Two middle changes suffice to restore nondecreasing order.
